chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Suleyman Al-Ja'fary who said:

I heard Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) saying regarding the Statement of Allah, Blessed and High: 'When they spend the night in what displeases Him in speech,' he said: 'It means So-and-so and So-and-so, and Abu Ubaydah ibn Al-Jarrah.'

key_terms.أَبُو عُبَيْدَةَ بْنَ الْجَرَّاحِ: Abu Ubaydah ibn Al-Jarrah (a companion of the Prophet)

ai.seo_question: Who does the Imam identify as the subjects of the verse 'Ith yubayyituna' in Surah An-Nisa?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam Al-Rida (peace be upon him) provides a specific exegetical application of Surah An-Nisa, verse 108, identifying the 'prominent companions' (Fuqaaha) who spent the night in speech displeasing to Allah as Abu Bakr, Umar, and Abu Ubaydah ibn Al-Jarrah. This interpretation highlights the Shia scholarly view that these key figures engaged in significant nocturnal deliberations or disputes, the content of which was not fully pleasing to divine will, thereby linking Quranic revelation directly to early Islamic political and scholarly history.
